recommendation.executive_summary: Recommend Architecture B — Cached Reads (API → Redis → PostgreSQL). Under the specified 500 RPS workload, it satisfies all mandatory constraints with a predicted p95 latency of 7.2ms (heuristic uncertainty bounds [7.1, 7.4] ms) at an estimated monthly cost of $176.00.
decision_rationale: Selected based on optimal balance under stated preferences (Cost: 30%, Latency: 50%, Simplicity: 20%).
Meets hard constraints: Achieves p95 latency of 7.2ms (target <= 100.0ms) at $176.00/mo (budget <= $250.00/mo).
Effective read caching (84.8% hit rate) shields the database connection pool, sustaining 501.6 RPS with 27.5% DB utilization.
main_trade_offs: Added operational complexity of Redis cache management, cache invalidation, and potential stale reads during write bursts.
Monthly cost is ~$43.00 higher than Architecture A due to the dedicated Redis instance.

rejection_reasons: Lower multi-objective score compared to Architecture B — Cached Reads (API → Redis → PostgreSQL).
rejected_alternatives.trade_off_vs_winner: Architecture A — Simple (API → PostgreSQL) exhibits higher latency or infrastructure overhead under the evaluated 500.0 RPS load profile.

rejected_alternatives.architecture_name: Architecture C — Async Processing (API → Queue → Worker → PostgreSQL)
rejection_reasons: Lower multi-objective score compared to Architecture B — Cached Reads (API → Redis → PostgreSQL).
rejected_alternatives.trade_off_vs_winner: Architecture C — Async Processing (API → Queue → Worker → PostgreSQL) exhibits higher latency or infrastructure overhead under the evaluated 500.0 RPS load profile.

evidence_limitations: Container-level isolation was used for benchmarks; bare-metal hypervisor contention was not simulated.
conditions_for_change: If read ratio drops below 60%, Redis caching benefits decrease and direct transactional database routing becomes more cost-effective.
If incoming traffic exceeds 650 RPS, direct PostgreSQL saturates 2 vCPU quotas, requiring horizontal read replicas or asynchronous ingestion queues.
If monthly infrastructure budget is capped below $150/mo, Architecture A (direct PostgreSQL without cache) is the only viable candidate.

assumed_parameters: Monthly infrastructure cost model: API container $30/mo, 2 vCPU PostgreSQL $70/mo, Redis $43/mo, Queue/Worker $53/mo.
Network inter-process transit latency: ~0.5ms inter-container overhead assumption.
Cache hit rate heuristic: 85% for read-heavy workloads when cache tier is present.
